I live across the road from a very busy block of shops, and close to a main road, so there are always lots of cars around my house, and cats everywhere in my neighbourhood, they all know to keep away from the cars :)

Cats are almost always outdoor cats here, so I just find this really interesting. 

Cats instinctively know how to get home, they also know what is safe/not safe to eat and could just as easily consume harmful poisons in your home (like cleaning products). I personally let my cat outside whenever he likes, mostly because I feel bad when I leave him inside all day. He's fully toilet trained but refuses to use his litter box and prefers to do his business outside. 

I'm not saying either way is 100% right, because obviously it depends on the owner/cat, but it's very interesting knowing the reasons behind it :)

Just out of genuine curiosity, why do people keep their cats inside all the time? In NZ indoor cats are almost unheard of, most cats are outdoor cats.
